findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The Go auto-linting paragraph mostly matches the supplied go-lint.ts. `fmt` runs only on the edited file. `run` targets `.` from the edited file's directory, so it checks the whole package. The diagnostic context says findings may predate the edit and that sibling files were not auto-fixed. `--path-prefix` supports the claim that findings identify their source files. I found no blocking errors. Some nearby general statements are looser than the Go behavior, and the supplied context can't fully confirm two details.

The general auto-linting text conflicts with the Go-specific paragraph. 'Usually nothing — the linter auto-fixes quietly' is followed by 'Go lint findings are not auto-fixed.' Go users get findings that are never auto-fixed, and those findings can predate the edit. Consider saying the auto-fix claim excludes Go, or moving the Go note next to the 'What you see' line.

'If a linter isn't installed, it's silently skipped' is not clearly true for Go. In go-lint.ts, a failed `fmt` or `run` produces a warning like 'golangci-lint fmt failed: …', or 'Go lint could not run: …' if an exception is thrown. A missing Safeword Go config also produces a visible warning. The supplied context doesn't show how a missing golangci-lint binary is handled (that's in goLintProcess), so it's unclear whether that case is actually silent.

'Check-only lint' assumes `config.args`, built in go-lint/config.js, never adds `--fix`. That file wasn't supplied. The `run` call in go-lint.ts adds no fix flag, and its diagnostic text says sibling files were not auto-fixed, which supports the claim.
